description.narrative: The project Inclusive Education for All works to realize the inclusivity of the regular school system by promoting the right to education for children with disabilities and ensuring public schools address special educational needs to provide an accommodative learning environment on an equal basis with non-disabled peers, in alignment with UNCRPD Articles 24 and 9, mainly focusing on: (1) Strengthening the technical capacity of 90 Regular and Special Needs Education (SNE) teachers, school management staff, and education experts (disaggregated by gender) through structured training and practical sessions; (2) enhancing physical accessibility in 15 selected primary and secondary schools through professional accessibility audits and model modification interventions; (3) developing and distributing accessible educational materials and adaptive technologies (e.g., Braille paper, digital recorders, and talking software) to 300 needy students with disabilities; (4) ensuring the active involvement of parents, caretakers, and community-based organizations (CBOs) in the placement and academic progress of 2,500 children with disabilities within the regular school system; and (5) reaching 200 duty-bearers, including government officials and law enforcement, through targeted advocacy and sensitization sessions.
